assumptions: PS1, PS2, PS3, S1, S2, S3, and reset are modeled as discrete events because the NL describes them as triggers or signals rather than persistent numeric variables.
hbrg is encoded as an integer output with 0 for stop, 1 for upward drive, and -1 for downward drive.
The immediate next-destination check is represented by the floor states responding immediately to subsequent request events; no request queue or stored outstanding-request memory was specified.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

canonical_scenario_results.description: default-init: dispatches to F1 stopped, then PS2 drives upward to MU2, S2 stops at F2, and the immediate next PS3 request continues upward to MU3.
canonical_scenario_results.name: default_init_f1_to_f2_then_continue_up

canonical_scenario_results.description: default-init: from F1, PS3 drives upward to MU3, S3 stops at F3, then PS2 requests downward travel to MD2 and S2 stops at F2.
canonical_scenario_results.name: default_init_f1_to_f3_then_down_to_f2

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from reachable stopped F2, PS1 must enter downward MD1 and S1 arrival must stop at F1.
canonical_scenario_results.name: hot_start_f2_down_to_f1

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from reachable stopped F3, PS1 must choose MD1 downward travel rather than the MD2/F2 branch.
canonical_scenario_results.name: hot_start_f3_direct_down_to_f1

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: reset from an upward motion state must force F1 stopped regardless of outstanding request context.
canonical_scenario_results.name: reset_forces_motion_up_to_f1

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: reset from a downward motion state must force F1 stopped regardless of outstanding request context.
canonical_scenario_results.name: reset_forces_motion_down_to_f1

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: reset from a non-F1 stopped floor state must force the controller back to F1 stopped.
canonical_scenario_results.name: reset_forces_floor_state_to_f1

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with no request or arrival event, a stopped floor state should not make a phantom transition and should keep hbrg in the stop condition.
canonical_scenario_results.name: no_event_stays_stopped_at_floor

evidence: DSL states: F1, F2, F3, MU2, MU3, MD1, MD2.
DSL transitions include F1->MU2:PS2, F1->MU3:PS3, F2->MU3:PS3, F2->MD1:PS1, F3->MD1:PS1, F3->MD2:PS2.
DSL arrival transitions include MU2->F2:S2, MU3->F3:S3, MD1->F1:S1, MD2->F2:S2.
DSL reset transition: ! * -> F1 :: reset.
State enter actions set hbrg=0 for floors, hbrg=1 for upward motion, and hbrg=-1 for downward motion.
findings.summary: The DSL closely matches the NL-described elevator FSM: all named floor and motion states are present, initial state is F1, reset forces F1, request-triggered motion transitions and sensor-triggered arrival transitions are represented, and hbrg distinguishes stop/up/down conditions.

evidence: Grounding map lists all seven required leaf states as required with high confidence.
Grounding map lists PS1/PS2/PS3, S1/S2/S3, and reset as required events.
Grounding map lists all request and arrival transitions as required.
inspect_model_to_json_summary reports 7 leaf states, 18 transitions including forced reset expansions, 7 events, 1 variable, and 7 actions.
five_component_summary is empty, but the bounded NL/DSL/grounding/simulation evidence is sufficient for review.
findings.summary: Required model components are substantively covered despite the provided five_component_summary being empty: states, transitions, events, and output action behavior are all represented in the DSL and grounding map.

evidence: Grounding assumption: 'The immediate next-destination check is represented by the floor states responding immediately to subsequent request events; no request queue or stored outstanding-request memory was specified.'
Simulation scenario default_init_f1_to_f2_then_continue_up passes: F1 -> MU2 -> F2 -> MU3 on PS2, S2, PS3.
NL says reset ignores outstanding request context, but does not specify queue semantics or persistence rules for outstanding requests.
findings.summary: No blocking coverage gap is evident. The only abstraction is that the 'immediate next-destination check' is represented by stopped floor states accepting the next request event, rather than by an explicit queue or decision substate; this is consistent with the grounding assumption and the NL does not require stored request memory.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary has blocking_count=0 and advisory_count=1.
Diagnostic: W_UNREFERENCED_VAR: Variable 'hbrg' does not affect any transition guard.
NL identifies hbrg as an output that distinguishes upward drive, downward drive, and stop conditions.
DSL uses hbrg only in state enter actions, consistent with output semantics.
findings.summary: The advisory W_UNREFERENCED_VAR on hbrg is acceptable because hbrg is modeled as a pure output, not as an internal guard variable. No unjustified warning-driven repair is needed.
